correctness.rationale: The independent uniform-within-color matching coupling proves C_a+C_b <=st C_(a+b). Deletion proves monotone C_m <=st C_(m+1). Conditioning on any isolated chord splits the rest into independent arcs, so its conditional crossing distribution is dominated by the unconditioned one. Summation over all candidate isolated chords gives Cov(I_n,g(C_n))<=0 for any increasing g, with strictness when g strictly increasing. Exact first moments and oriented-arc counting give the covariance sum and a Vandermonde ratio bound gives the asymptotic expansion. The bundled program passed 1037 exact assertions, including full matching enumeration through n=7; infinite claims rely on the written proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem for all increasing transforms is stronger than a single negative covariance. Published marginal distributions, fixed-small-crossing enumeration and asymptotic component-limit laws do not by themselves entail finite-sample stochastic order under isolate size bias. The random two-color coupling supplies the missing comparison.

value.rationale: The random chord intersection graph has natural edge count C_n and isolate count I_n. A universal negative covariance for every increasing transform of C_n is a distribution-wide joint dependence property beyond marginal laws and much more informative than a scalar covariance. The isolate split creates an exact k-dependent crossing deficit and quantitative n/3-scale covariance, identifying a geometric suppression mechanism and enabling model-specific comparison bounds.
